content:
iOS 27 continues Apple's trend of giving you more freedom to customize your iPhone's Lock Screen. This year brings additional customization options, wallpaper settings, and other features.

Extended wallpapers

iOS 27 brings new Apple Intelligence editing features to the Photos app, including a redesigned Clean Up tool, as well as a Recompose feature. Another new option is Extend, which uses intelligence to expand your photos, making it easy to adjust aspect ratio, fix a crooked horizon, or simply add more space at the edges.

As shown above, the Extend feature will also come to the Lock Screen in iOS 27. If a photo doesn't fit your iPhone's aspect ratio, or isn't cropped well for a wallpaper, iOS 27 will automatically suggest using Extend to fix it.

Extend uses AI to generate additional content at the edges of your photos, giving you more flexibility when setting your iPhone wallpaper.

Make your own wallpaper

iOS 27 brings major improvements to Image Playground, Apple's AI image generation app. The changes to Image Playground will also extend to your iPhone's Lock Screen. You can now use Image Playground to generate wallpapers directly from the Settings or Lock Screen wallpaper picker.

In the wallpaper picker, you'll see a new Image Playground option. This feature will create stylized versions of images from your Photos library, such as Nostalgic Illustration and Animation.

You can also start from scratch, describing what you want with natural language to create a custom wallpaper.

Move the clock

iOS 27 finally lets you shrink the clock on your iPhone's Lock Screen. While Apple has let you customize the size of the clock for years, iOS 27 goes a step further, now letting you move the Lock Screen clock to the top widget row.

This frees up more Lock Screen space, so you can see more of your wallpaper. The tradeoff, of course, is that you can't easily check the time at a glance from across the room. But for many people, the point of the Lock Screen is to show off a wallpaper, and iOS 27 makes that easier.

Swipe away Now Playing widget

In iOS 27, you can now swipe away the Now Playing widget that appears on your iPhone's Lock Screen. Even if you dismiss the Now Playing widget, whatever you're listening to will keep playing.

If you frequently hit the Lock Screen's Now Playing widget by accident, this is a very useful feature.

Wrap up

iOS 27 is now available to developers and public beta testers and will launch later this year. What do you think of the new Lock Screen customization features in iOS 27? Let us know in the comments section below.
